title: T1657 — Financial Theft
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Financial Theft with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: Phishing email steals clerk credentials
steps.caption: The attacker sends a convincing sign-in page to a finance clerk. The clerk types the password into the fake page. Nothing visible breaks, and no alert fires yet. Evidence: none at first - later, the phishing message itself in mail trace logs
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Sign-in from an attacker VPS
steps.caption: The attacker logs into the mailbox from a virtual private server (VPS) in another country. The login looks impossible: the clerk was in one country minutes before. Evidence: an impossible-travel sign-in risk event, a new IP address, and a new browser user agent
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Hidden inbox rule buries invoices
steps.caption: The attacker creates an inbox rule that moves any mail with words like “invoice”, “payment”, or “bank” into a hidden folder. The clerk stops seeing vendor emails. Evidence: a New-InboxRule event in the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log (UAL)
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Weeks of silent thread reading

steps.title: Look-alike domain and fake bank details
steps.caption: The attacker registers a look-alike domain and emails the treasury team from it, posing as the vendor. The message says the vendor has a new bank account and repeats details from the real thread. Evidence: a DNS query for the look-alike domain, and an email from a newly registered sender domain
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Treasury approves and executes the wire
steps.caption: Treasury compares the mail thread, sees no reason to doubt it, and pays the invoice to the “new” account. The bank confirms the debit. Evidence: a new payee record and a first-time payment that beat the fraud checks
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: SOC links three signals
steps.caption: The SOC correlates three alerts: a finance inbox rule, a query to a look-alike domain, and a new payee. Each alert alone looks small. Together they tell one story. Evidence: a correlated case in the SIEM with all three signals
steps.defender: WAF, reverse-proxy and application logs record the request, payload and backend behavior.

steps.title: Recall and response
steps.caption: The SOC calls the bank fraud line to request a recall, removes the inbox rule, resets the clerk’s credentials, blocks the look-alike domain, and re-verifies the vendor’s real bank details by phone. Evidence: recall ticket, rule deletion event, credential reset, and a proxy block for the domain
